notes: Swahili has no grammatical gender; people (including {name}) take class 1/2 agreement, which is gender-neutral. Placeholders for buildings, warriors and items would need noun-class agreement, so those sentences use a colon or an invariant verb (Ujenzi umekamilika: {building}).

Generated names need generatedNames: "noun-first". Second parts carry their own correct -a connector (Kilele cha, Bonde la, Njia ya, Mto wa) and first parts are bare nouns (Radi, Chuma, Ukungu), so every pair agrees: Kilele cha Radi, Lango la Chuma.
Swahili uses only ASCII Latin letters, so it fits the bundled Latin-1 fonts.
Plurals use one/other as Intl.PluralRules("sw") gives; Swahili puts the noun before the number (wapiganaji #).

The Japanese statutory pages are translated in full into Swahili; the support page links them by their Japanese titles, as other languages do (pages.support.26 triggers a script warning for that reason).
The ui.s_have_bced00a61e fragment is no longer used by code; ui.your_purchase_been_delivered_6f88dee143 was written so that the fragment (wote) reads naturally if it is.
